title: Open-DeBias: Toward Mitigating Open-Set Bias in Language Models
findings: The proposed Open-DeBias method significantly mitigates religious bias in language models. When applied to DeBERTa-V3-Large on the BBQ dataset, it increased accuracy in ambiguous religious contexts from 0.45 (BMBI baseline) to 0.94, and maintained high accuracy (0.99) in disambiguated contexts. On the CrowS-Pairs benchmark, the method brought the bias score for religion closer to the ideal of 50, indicating a reduction in stereotypical associations.

measurement_description: The benchmark measures the mitigation of stereotypical biases in multiple-choice question-answering contexts related to religion. It assesses model performance in both ambiguous contexts, where a neutral answer is correct, and disambiguated contexts, where enough information is provided for a correct, non-stereotypical answer.
